2026Q2.en: In Q2 2026, Los Angeles occupancy rose to 95.8%, up 0.4 points from Q1, as tenants absorbed a net 1.23M sf, led by LA South (+1.98M sf in the quarter). Asking rents slipped to $15.83/sf/yr, down 1.4% QoQ and 8.3% below Q3 2024. New supply is thin: 0.76M sf delivered this year and 4.4M sf under construction, about 0.6% of stock. With little new space coming, occupancy should stay tight, and rents look more likely to stabilize than to rebound soon.

Inland Empire occupancy fell to 91.2% in Q2 2026, down 0.3 points QoQ, as tenants vacated a net 1.54M sf (3.81M sf so far this year). IE West accounts for most of this year's losses, and IE East has the highest vacancy at 11.0%. Asking rents edged up 0.9% QoQ to $12.40/sf/yr but are 9.4% below a year ago and 17% below Q3 2024. Space under construction rose to 4.8M sf from 3.3M sf last quarter. Rents are likely to stay under pressure until move-outs slow.

Dallas–Fort Worth absorbed a net 9.03M sf in Q2 2026, the most of the five metros, lifting occupancy to 91.9% (up 0.2 points QoQ). Asking rents rose 5.5% QoQ to $9.19/sf/yr, 14.4% above a year ago. Alliance led demand with 3.9M sf absorbed this year. The risk is supply: 13.6M sf has been delivered this year and 29.8M sf is still under construction, about 2.9% of stock, so further occupancy gains depend on demand keeping pace.

Chicago occupancy held at 95.2% in Q2 2026, and vacancy has stayed between 4.7% and 4.8% for two years. Net absorption picked up to 3.30M sf in the quarter, and asking rents rose 2.0% QoQ to $7.55/sf/yr, roughly flat versus a year ago. Construction has doubled from 6.8M sf a year ago to 13.9M sf, a third of it in the I-80 corridor. The market is steady, but the growing pipeline is worth watching.

Northern New Jersey occupancy was 91.7% in Q2 2026, unchanged from Q1. Net absorption slowed to 0.26M sf after a strong first quarter, bringing the year to 2.34M sf, ahead of the 1.92M sf delivered. Asking rents are the highest of the five metros at $17.72/sf/yr, up 1.6% QoQ but 5.8% below Q3 2024. The Port Region is the weak spot at 11.6% vacancy.
